Traditional Scottish Oat Bannocks

Served at: Imbolc Day Celebration · St. Andrew's Day

Makes 6-8 bannocksPrep 15 minCook 20-25 min

Bannocks are simple, unleavened flatbreads with a long history in Scotland, often made with oats or barley. They are a comforting and versatile staple, perfect for celebrating Imbolc as a symbol of hearth and home, marking the return of light and the promise of spring. They are also a fitting traditional food for St. Andrew's Day, Scotland's national day, embodying the country's culinary heritage.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups (150g) medium oatmeal (or quick-cooking oats pulsed in a food processor until finer)
  • 1/2 cup (60g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 cup (55g) cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
  • 3/4 cup (180ml) buttermilk (or milk with 1 tablespoon lemon juice, let sit 5 min)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, whisk together the oatmeal, all-purpose flour, baking soda, and salt.
  2. Add the cold butter pieces to the dry ingredients. Using your fingertips or a pastry blender, rub the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
  3. Make a well in the center and pour in the buttermilk. Mix with a fork until just combined and a soft dough forms. Be careful not to overmix.
  4. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Gently knead for just a few seconds until it comes together.
  5. Pat or roll the dough into a round about 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) thick.
  6. Cut the round into 6-8 wedges (like a scone) or use a 3-inch (7.5 cm) round cutter to make individual bannocks.
  7. Heat a heavy-bottomed skillet or griddle over medium heat. Lightly grease if necessary.
  8. Cook the bannocks for 5-7 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. The internal temperature should be around 200°F (93°C).
  9. Transfer to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • Serve warm with butter, honey, jam, or a savory accompaniment like cheese or smoked salmon.
  • For a more rustic bannock, you can use only medium oatmeal and omit the all-purpose flour, though you may need slightly less liquid.
  • Avoid overworking the dough; a light touch ensures tender bannocks. Overmixing can make them tough.
